title: NDPBridge: Enabling Cross-Bank Coordination in Near-DRAM-Bank Processing Architectures
problem: Near-DRAM-bank NDP architectures suffer from physical isolation preventing fast and direct cross-bank communication, limiting their usage to simple parallel patterns and causing severe load imbalance when banks contain data with diverse computation loads.
motivation: Enabling efficient cross-bank communication and dynamic load balancing is essential to unlock the full efficiency potential of near-DRAM-bank NDP architectures for diverse data-intensive applications.
method: NDPBridge adds specialized hardware bridges within the DRAM memory structure to enable processing units near different banks to communicate and coordinate their workloads. It preserves existing DDR memory connections and protocols unchanged. The system distributes tasks across banks while being aware of how much data needs to move, and uses three techniques to reduce delays: hiding communication wait-time by doing other work simultaneously (latency hiding), routing traffic around congested paths (congestion avoidance), and reducing the amount of data that must transfer (traffic reduction).
key_novelty: NDPBridge embeds communication bridges in the DRAM hierarchy and pairs them with intelligent task scheduling to enable processing units near different banks to coordinate directly and balance computational load dynamically.
contributions: Hardware bridges integrated into DRAM hierarchy for cross-bank coordination without disrupting DDR protocols
Hierarchical and data-transfer-aware load balancing scheme
Task-based programming model for cross-bank NDP coordination
Optimizations for latency hiding, congestion avoidance, and traffic reduction
